Run a Bayesian hierarchical mixed model

Source: R/bayes_mm_run.R
bayes_mm_run.Rd

Runs a Bayesian mixed model with up to three conditions as fixed effects and any number of grouping factors (such as participants) as random effects, using the rstanarm package. You give it the names of the columns and it writes the model formula for you. This can take a few minutes.

Usage

bayes_mm_run(
  data,
  dvname,
  conditions,
  groups,
  f = NULL,
  mmtype = "intercept",
  binom = F,
  adapt_delta = 0.8,
  explore_browser = F,
  iter = 2000
)

Arguments

data

The data in long format, with a row for each observation.

dvname

The name of the column with the dependent variable.

conditions

A vector of up to three names of columns, the fixed effects. Factors (or text) and numeric variables can be used.

groups

A vector of names of columns with the grouping factors for the random effects, eg "pid".

f

A model formula (as text) to use instead of making one from conditions and groups.

mmtype

"intercept" (the default) for random intercepts, or "slopes" to have random slopes too.

binom

If TRUE, the dv is modelled as binomial, with a logit link (for 0/1 data). The default is a normal (gaussian) model.

adapt_delta

Defaults to 0.8. Raise it towards 1 if the model has convergence problems (it is slower).

explore_browser

If TRUE, open a browser window to explore the model with shinystan.

iter

The number of iterations for each chain. Default 2000.

Value

The model, a stanreg object from rstanarm. Pass it to bayes_mm(), bayes_mm_mainFX() or bayes_mm_interact().

Details

All of the conditions are crossed (a * b * c), and a random effect is added for each of the groups. With the default mmtype = "intercept" each group gets a random intercept ((1 | pid)); with "slopes" each group also gets random slopes for the conditions ((1 + a + b | pid)).

To avoid problems later on, punctuation and spaces in the names of the conditions, and in the levels of any condition that is a factor or text, are replaced by underscores (so "Not addressable" becomes "Not_addressable"), and text columns are turned into factors. This is done to a copy of your data, which is stored in the model (bmm$data). The conditions are cleaned in the same way, so when you ask for plots, use the cleaned names.

The model is run with the default priors of rstanarm::stan_glmer. The function also sets the R option mc.cores to the number of cores on your computer, so that the chains run in parallel.

See also

bayes_mm()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bmm <- bayes_mm_run(data = ad_data, dvname = "dprime",
                    conditions = c("adcon", "age", "tv"),
                    groups = c("pid", "dim"))
} # }
